title: Tagless LysoIP method for molecular profiling of lysosomal content in clinical samples
projectDescription: Lysosomes are implicated in a wide spectrum of human diseases including monogenic lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs), age-associated neurodegeneration and cancer. Profiling lysosomal content using tag-based lysosomal immunopurification (LysoIP) in cell and animal models allowed major discoveries in the field, however, studying lysosomal dysfunction in human patients remains a challenge. Here, we report the development of the tagless LysoIP method to enable rapid enrichment of lysosomes, via immunoisolation, using the endogenous integral lysosomal membrane protein TMEM192, directly from clinical samples and human cells. Isolated lysosomes are intact and suitable for subsequent multimodal omics analyses. To validate the utility of our approach, we employed the tagless LysoIP to enrich lysosomes from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) derived from fresh blood of patients with CLN3 Batten disease, a neurodegenerative LSD. Altogether, the tagless LysoIP provides a framework to study native lysosomes from patient samples, identify novel biomarkers and discover human-relevant disease mechanisms.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Cells stably expressing LysoTag or MockTag were cultured in the continued presence of puromycin (2 μg/ml) in 15 cm diameter dishes to 90% confluency. Cells were scraped into Potassium Phosphate Buffer Saline (KPBS) containing 1X Complete Protease Inhibitor cocktail and 1X PhosSTOP phosphatase inhibitor cocktail . An aliquot (5% by vol) of the cell suspension was removed and cells pelleted at 1500 x g and frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored at -80 °C for subsequent proteomic, lipidomic or metabolomic analysis. This fraction is termed the “whole cell extract”. The remaining cell suspension was homogenized using Isobiotec cell-breaker. Homogenates were cleared of debris by centrifugation at 1,500 × g for 2 min at 4 °C. The remainder of the supernatant containing cellular organelles was collected and transferred to a clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube containing 100 µL of 50% (by vol) slurry of anti-HA magnetic bead. The mixture was incubated at 4 °C for 5 min on an orbiter ensuring constant gentle agitation. After incubation, the tube containing the mixture was placed on a magnet for 30 s and the supernatant was removed. The beads were washed 3 times with ice cold KPBS, aliquoted and snap frozen in liquid nitrogen and stored in -80 °C until further processing for proteomic sample preparation. The lysosomes were eluted by adding 2% SDS Lysis buffer (2% SDS wt/vol) in 20mM HEPES pH 8.0 with protease and phosSTOP inhibitors. The eluates were further sonicated using Bioruptor sonication and estimated using BCA assay along with whole cell lysates. The sample were then reduced using 5mM final TCEP at 60oC and alkylated by adding 20mM final Iodoacetamide and incubated in dark for 30 minutes. The Whole cells and Lyso-IP samples were then processed using Strap assisted on-column digestion using Trypsin+Lys-C mix and the eluted peptides were vacuum dried and store in -80 freezer until further analysis.
dataProcessingProtocol: MS data acquisition and database searches: The Lyso-IP samples from wild type and LysoTAG HEK293 experiments were acquired on timsTOF-Pro mass spectrometer inline with EvoSep One LC system. Data acquired in dia-PASEF mode. The wild type HEK293 Lyso-IP experiment data acquired using tims-TOF SCP mass spectrometer inline with Evosep One LC system. PBMC lyso-IP experiments acquired on Orbitrap Exploris 480 coupled with Dionex ultimate 3000 LC system in DIA-mode. iPSC Lyso-IP experiments acquired on Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometer coupled with Vanquish-Neo LC system and data acquired using narrow window DIA mode. All datasets were searched using DIA-NN 1.8.1 against Human Uniprot database and downstream data analysis carried out using Perseus software suite and data visualization is carried out using CURTAIN tool.
